title: J1 — Born abroad
description: A Lao baby gets his first vaccines in Thailand and leaves with signed paper cards. The prose of this scenario is docs/journeys.md, section J1.

steps.title: A Lao baby is born in Thailand
steps.headline: Somsack gets his birth vaccines in a Thai hospital — and the only thing that will cross the border with him is a pair of paper cards.

experiences.doing: Gives Hep B and BCG birth doses and prints two signed QR vaccine cards.
experiences.feeling: “He isn’t Thai, but he still needs a record he can take home.”

experiences.doing: Is born, and gets his Hep B and BCG birth doses within hours.
experiences.feeling: “Two small jabs, and a record that will follow him.”

experiences.doing: Gives birth away from home and receives two paper cards at discharge.
experiences.feeling: “Will anyone back home believe these papers?”

steps.painPoint: The baby has no Thai ID number, so his records would normally stay locked inside the Thai hospital’s system.
steps.enabler: A digitally signed QR card travels with the family — no ID number or database lookup needed.

handoff.summary: Two paper cards go home with Khamla

whatIf.scenario: The cards are lost on the way home.
whatIf.outcome: The doses still happened, but no proof travels. Lao clinicians must re-vaccinate or rely on memory.
